hints: The whole twist is one line: when dist[u] + w[u][v] beats dist[v], also set parent[v] = u. The last u that improved v is its tree parent.
The tree has at most n-1 edges - one into each reachable vertex other than s. So after Dijkstra, loop over v and write tree[parent[v]][v].
The input graph is DIRECTED (one-way roads), so the tree edge is written in one direction only, unlike an MST matrix.
source: Reconstruction of the DSA Lab Week 4 modification question
title: Dijkstra: print the shortest-path tree as a matrix
